title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
claim: POM-based all-inorganic open frameworks are assembled either by self-polymerization of POM clusters through shared vertices, edges, or faces, or by joining POM clusters with additional inorganic cations.
explanation: The review groups known routes into these two strategies. Self-polymerization is illustrated by a 154-nuclearity molybdate ring that connects to six neighbors through Mo–O–Mo bonds. The linker route uses transition-metal, lanthanide, or alkali/alkaline-earth cations and is the more common construction across later Nb, Mo, V, and W examples.
scope: All-inorganic open frameworks built from polyoxoniobate, polyoxomolybdate, polyoxovanadate, or polyoxotungstate secondary building units.
conditions: Aqueous, hydrothermal, or related solution conditions; exact pH, temperature, and cation identity are system-dependent.
caveats: Adding extra metal linkers frequently produces dense rather than open packing, so porosity is not guaranteed by the linker strategy alone.
